papers.title: Chikungunya virus uses the tetraspanins CD63, CD9, and CD151 to replicate in human synovial fibroblasts.
papers.summary: Chikungunya virus causes lasting joint pain, but host factors for joint-cell infection are largely unknown. Silencing tetraspanins CD63, CD9, and CD151 in human synovial fibroblasts reduced replicon activity, intracellular genome accumulation, and progeny production, while MXRA8 mediated entry — identifying tetraspanins as CHIKV host factors and candidate antiviral targets in joint tissue.

papers.title: Antigen-specific regulatory T cells eliminate cognate CD4 effector T cells through perforin, granzyme B, and Bim.
papers.summary: Regulatory T cells eliminate cognate CD4 effector T cells through a "double-lock" co-activation mechanism: simultaneous peptide-MHC II recognition induces perforin and granzyme B in Tregs, while responders upregulate Bim via TCR signaling. Deleting Gzmb, Prf1, or Bcl2l11 abrogates killing; airway-inflammation models and human assays confirm cognate-antigen-dependent cytotoxicity.

papers.title: Activation of TREM2 via single-domain antibodies improves synaptic and cognitive function in 5×FAD mice.
papers.summary: Two TREM2-activating single-domain antibodies, 10c11 and 10e12, injected into 5×FAD mice activated microglia and rescued cognitive deficits. 10e12 reduced amyloid plaques and preserved synaptic function; 10c11 protected synapses without lowering plaque burden. Both reduced C1q levels, showing TREM2 activation exerts multifaceted, mechanism-distinct effects with Alzheimer's therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Epstein-Barr virus gp350 neutralizing epitopes define distinct sites of vulnerability.
papers.summary: Researchers isolated human monoclonal antibodies from EBV-seropositive donors against gp350, the viral attachment glycoprotein. Antibody 1a12 protected humanized mice by markedly reducing viral load and pathology, and structural mapping defined three antigenic clusters on gp350, including a distal-domain epitope neutralizing via a post-attachment mechanism — informing next-generation EBV vaccines and antibody therapies.

papers.title: GmBBX13 and GmBBX4a/b antagonistically regulate GmCML19 transcription to fine-tune leaf senescence in soybean.
papers.journal: Journal of genetics and genomics = Yi chuan xue bao
papers.summary: GmBBX13 delays soybean leaf senescence by repressing GmCML19, while its interacting partners GmBBX4a/b promote senescence by activating the same gene. The antagonistic B-box module co-regulates roughly 4,700 target genes, revealing a molecular mechanism that fine-tunes senescence timing and offering strategies to extend grain-filling and improve soybean yield.

papers.title: Drosophila midgut tumor-induced insulin resistance systemically remodels lymph gland hematopoiesis during cancer cachexia.
papers.summary: In a Drosophila midgut-tumor cachexia model, tumors remodel the lymph gland hematopoietic niche and circulating hemocytes. Tumor- and hemocyte-derived Impl2, an insulin antagonist, suppresses insulin signaling in the niche-progenitor microenvironment, shrinking the niche and driving blood-cell differentiation; depleting tumor Impl2 rescues cachectic phenotypes, linking tumor metabolism to systemic tissue wasting.

papers.title: Replication protein A1 from L. donovani interacts with RECQb via the C-terminal OB fold and stimulates its helicase activity on branched substrates.
papers.summary: Leishmania donovani RPA1 lacks the N-terminal domain eukaryotic RecQ helicases use to bind RPA, yet still stimulates LdRECQb unwinding. The interaction maps to RECQb's winged-helix domain and RPA1's C-terminal OB fold 3, enhances unwinding of duplexes, Holliday junctions, and G-quadruplexes, and supports regressed-fork restoration — a prokaryotic-like, functionally conserved mechanism.

papers.title: NFKBIB methylation by SETD3 controls NF-κB-mediated interferon activation during viral infection.
papers.summary: The methyltransferase SETD3 positively regulates type I interferon signaling during viral infection. SETD3 methylates NFKBIB at lysine 235, reinforcing its p62 binding and autophagic degradation, which frees NF-κB for nuclear translocation and downstream antiviral gene transcription — revealing SETD3-mediated nonhistone methylation as a potential antiviral control point.

papers.title: Myocardial mitochondrial morphology and oxidative phosphorylation capacity in wild-type transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
papers.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
papers.summary: In endomyocardial biopsies from 52 wild-type transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy patients, only about 48% of cardiomyocyte mitochondria were morphologically normal and oxidative phosphorylation capacity was reduced. Mitochondrial area correlated with respiratory capacity, and greater wall thickness tracked with fewer, smaller, less functional mitochondria, but amyloid-load measures did not independently associate with mitochondrial function.

papers.title: Auto-S-fatty acylation of PKM2 regulates its tetramerization and glycolytic metabolism in cancer cells.
papers.summary: Pyruvate kinase M2 undergoes auto-S-fatty acylation at a conserved cysteine (Cys474), preferentially incorporating palmitate and stearate. The modification destabilizes the active tetramer, suppresses pyruvate kinase activity, and reshapes glycolytic intermediates; the non-acylatable C474S mutant enhances mitochondrial respiration and impairs lung-cancer growth, linking fatty-acid availability to aerobic glycolysis and tumor growth.

papers.title: A Thieno[3,2-D] pyrimidine class of p110α/GDH1 dual inhibitor SBS-873 suppresses TNBC growth by inhibiting PI3K/mTOR signaling and inducing ferroptosis through glutathione depletion.
papers.summary: SBS-873, a thieno[3,2-d]pyrimidine dual inhibitor of p110α and GDH1, suppresses PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling while depleting glutathione and impairing GPX4, driving ferroptosis in triple-negative breast cancer. It selectively killed TNBC cells, spared non-tumorigenic mammary cells, and reduced xenograft growth without observable toxicity — a first-in-class metabolic-therapy candidate.

papers.title: Epitranscriptomic regulation of Notch signaling.
papers.summary: This review proposes a four-step framework for judging whether RNA modifications directly regulate Notch transcripts: site-resolved mapping, modifier- or reader-dependent fate change, altered signaling output, and rescue/epistasis. Reader identity determines m6A directionality — YTHDF2 promotes decay while YTHDF1 and IGF2BP readers enhance translation or stability — across developmental, cancer, and immune contexts.

papers.title: In vitro validation of a CRISPR/Cas9 guide RNA targeting COL1A1 gene by cleavage assay.
papers.summary: A CRISPR/Cas9 guide targeting COL1A1 exon 2 — a gene frequently mutated in osteogenesis imperfecta — was validated in vitro as a ribonucleoprotein against PCR substrates from five human cell lines. Cleavage efficiencies ranged 58.8–68.8%, supporting this cell-free assay as a pre-cellular validation step toward knockout models of osteogenesis imperfecta.

papers.title: Reversing liver sinusoidal endothelial aging restores clearance of amyloid-beta and LDL.
papers.summary: In aged rats, the soluble guanylate cyclase activator cinaciguat restored liver sinusoidal endothelial fenestration, halved circulating amyloid-beta 40, and reversed age-related LDL increases. Cinaciguat also revived aged LSEC secretion of HB-EGF, restoring hepatocyte LDLR/LRP1 surface expression and uptake — identifying intercellular LSEC-hepatocyte crosstalk and a candidate therapy for age-related amyloid-beta and LDL accumulation.

papers.title: Activation of Cu(II)-reducing ability of monoamine neurotransmitters triggered by amyloid-β fibrillization.
papers.summary: Fibrillized amyloid-beta 1-40 enhances copper reduction by the monoamine neurotransmitters serotonin and dopamine — and the accompanying hydrogen peroxide production — whereas monomeric Aβ 1-40 inhibits both. The effect likely reflects fibril Cu(I)-binding capability absent in monomers, partially explaining how Aβ aggregation promotes oxidative stress near synapses in Alzheimer's disease.

papers.title: Cryo-EM structure of human TMEM45A with a bound 2-Hydroxypalmitate.
papers.summary: Single-particle cryo-EM at 3.27 Å reveals human TMEM45A — an orphan seven-transmembrane protein highly expressed in keratinocytes and hypoxic cancer cells, contributing to metastasis and chemoresistance — as a homotetramer whose first six transmembrane helices form a central hydrophobic tunnel binding 2-hydroxypalmitate, suggesting a lipid-binding function and structural target in tumors.

papers.title: Phenotypic divergence persists despite substantial gene flow in a Mimulus guttatus metapopulation.
papers.summary: Twelve Mimulus guttatus populations on two nearby Oregon ridges show strong phenotypic divergence in flowering time, stem height, and trichomes — exceeding expectations from genetic structure despite substantial gene flow. Weak or non-significant contemporary selection gradients suggest past selection shaped these differences, demonstrating local adaptation at microgeographic scales under temporally heterogeneous environments.

papers.title: From timekeeping to divisions-Molecular links between circadian rhythms and cell cycle.
papers.summary: This review surveys molecular links between circadian rhythms and the cell cycle — two fundamental oscillators whose coupling outcomes depend on coupling directionality, oscillator periods, and the number and strength of connections. It discusses implications for mammalian stem-cell proliferation and differentiation, framing coupled-oscillator dynamics as an emerging regulatory layer in cell physiology.

papers.title: Sunflower oil-loaded lycopene protects intestinal barrier integrity following traumatic brain injury.
papers.summary: Sunflower-oil-loaded lycopene reduced intestinal and cerebral injury in traumatic-brain-injury mice by restoring intestinal barrier genes (occludin, ZO-1), lowering inflammatory and tissue-injury biomarkers, and modulating linoleic-acid, sphingolipid, and tryptophan metabolism. Associated microbiome differences in human TBI patients support anti-inflammatory, gut-mediated protection as a potential adjunctive therapy after brain injury.

papers.title: Yohimbine attenuates bleomycin-induced skin fibrosis by modulating the PI3K/Akt-MAPK signaling: an integrated network pharmacology and in vivo study.
papers.summary: Integrating network pharmacology with a bleomycin-induced mouse model, yohimbine attenuated skin fibrosis at 2.5–5 mg/kg, suppressing pro-fibrotic (CCN2, α-SMA, vimentin) and inflammatory markers, restoring antifibrotic HGF and NRF2-pathway antioxidants, and reducing collagen deposition — likely via PI3K/Akt-MAPK modulation — a potential lead given no FDA-approved antifibrotic therapies exist.

papers.title: The deubiquitinating enzyme USP42 promotes lung adenocarcinoma progression through PTGS2.
papers.summary: USP42, overexpressed in lung adenocarcinoma and associated with advanced stage and poor survival, physically interacts with and deubiquitinates PTGS2, stabilizing it from proteasomal degradation. Knockdown suppressed proliferation, invasion, EMT, and PD-L1 expression while alleviating CD8 T-cell exhaustion in mice; forced PTGS2 expression rescued these phenotypes, establishing USP42 as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Effects of decalcification with 10% nitric acid solution and EDTA on Safranin O staining and aggrecan immunohistochemistry.
papers.summary: Comparing decalcification protocols across mouse strains and rat paws, EDTA (room temperature or 35°C) outperformed 10% nitric acid for Safranin O staining and aggrecan immunohistochemistry, which showed strain-dependent, significantly reduced labeling after acid decalcification. EDTA's gentler mineral removal better preserves glycosaminoglycan staining and aggrecan antigenicity — informing histological protocol selection.

papers.title: Molecular heterogeneity and diagnostic performance of phenotype-driven multigene panel testing in patients with marfanoid habitus.
papers.summary: A custom NGS panel for marfanoid habitus identified variants in 28 of 51 analyzed patients (54.9% diagnostic yield; 31.3% for clinically definitive cases), including four FBN1 cases. Higher systemic scores and ROC analysis (AUC 0.80) for FBN1-related cases support phenotype-driven multigene panel testing as an effective diagnostic strategy.
